text: Ilse Brandt, nine kyu. You are the one Hana brought in, so you will not have read anything yet.
I have read all of it. Four books on the opening and two on the endgame, and I am nine kyu, which I would like you to think about carefully before you decide reading is the answer.
The sequences are correct. I am the part that goes wrong.
Do you want a league game? It goes on the board either way.
Fine. I will be here. Page ninety-one.
You went outside the book. There is no follow-up written for that, because it is not good.
It also beat me. I am recording both of those facts and I have not reconciled them.
That was the standard sequence, and it worked, and I will take no credit for it.
Read the first forty pages. Then come back and beat me with something that is not in them.
Six now. I have read four books on the opening and two on the endgame and I am nine kyu, and you have read nothing.
I have decided the books are not the problem. I read them the way you would read a timetable -- to know what happens, not to work out why.
So. From now on I am going to try to be wrong on purpose, occasionally, and see what happens. Do not congratulate me, it is humiliating.
Three games. I have been keeping the record, obviously, and I have noticed something and I would rather say it than keep noticing it.
You play moves that are not in any book, and roughly half of them are better than the book. I do not know what to do with that.
